For platform-team. Read 2026-10-07 07:12 to 07:19 (UTC). scheck test.
Trigger        incident
This is not incident response. scheck does not look for signs of intrusion, and evidence read from a
possibly compromised system cannot be trusted. This report lists weaknesses in what scheck could
read; it cannot tell you whether you are safe now or how the incident happened. For that you need an
incident responder; what this report can do is list weaknesses to close.
Method         rules only: a fixed checklist per asset type, no model, no hypotheses. Reading only:
               nothing was probed, scanned, exploited or changed. Not a penetration test.
Authorization  none recorded. This run only read, with access you already hold; scheck requires a
               record only for probes and scans.
Handle with care: this report names people, accounts, internal hosts and services, and says where
weaknesses are. Keep it as private as a list of passwords. It is written for you, not for your
customers.

1  high  The macOS application firewall is disabled (macos) [fw.app_firewall_disabled]
   Observed      fw.global#1 (07:12, as deploy): Firewall is disabled. (State = 0)
   Severity      high: base medium, +1 exposure internet (assets.macos.context.exposure)
   Why here      You declared macos internet-facing (assets.macos.context.exposure).
   Fix           Turn the application firewall on in System Settings > Network > Firewall, or from
                 the command line.
                 Caveat: This is a per-application filter, not a packet filter; it does not replace
                   a network firewall.
                 Commands (review before running):
                   sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setglobalstate on

Accepted (not counted as open)
   low     Software updates are pending (macos): accepted by alice, no expiry: "the vendor ships
     updates monthly" (intent.accepted_risks[0]). Covers every instance of this id on this asset.
